knowledge_point.title: Identifying Parallel Lines Given in Standard Form

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $-5x+y=-1$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two distinct nonvertical lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of $-5x+y=-1$, convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-5x+y &= -1 \\
y &= 5x-1 \\
y &= 5x-1
\end{aligned}
$$

The slope is the coefficient of $x$, so the required slope is $5$.

Only $y=5x-2$ has slope $5$.

The line $y=5x-2$ has slope $5$ and $y$-intercept $-2$, different from $-1$. Therefore, it is a distinct parallel line.

$$
y=5x-2
$$
